title: Cognitive macro-components and plugin architecture

Complete a step only when its acceptance criteria have evidence; document blocked or skipped checks.
Keep at most one step in progress and point current_step to it; use null between steps.
Treat research proposals as hypotheses until a decision or experiment supports them.
Review public-contract, schema, configuration, and deployment compatibility before implementation.
constraints: Preserve Interface -> Event/Request -> Orchestrator -> Domain -> Service.
Keep domain business policy outside orchestrator infrastructure and provider plugins.
Keep the existing public event envelope compatible.
Extend macro capabilities through versioned local plugin contracts.
Preserve existing plugin formats through adapters before adding new manifest fields.
Use explicit prediction targets and observed outcomes; keep similarity and factual reliability distinct.
Leave unrelated working-tree changes and experimental code untouched.
Require user approval for merging, tags, and production deployment.

steps.title: Record the prototype architecture decisions
acceptance_criteria: Task scope, workspace ownership, lifecycle, limits, and persistence are explicit.
Provider, domain-policy, and workflow extension responsibilities remain distinct.
Plugin compatibility and deterministic capability-selection rules are specified.
Existing stateful service behavior and the stateless-service rule are explicitly addressed without silently changing project policy.
The first prediction target, baseline, feedback semantics, and prototype non-goals are recorded.
Research semantic relationships, runtime dependencies, feedback cycles, and orchestrator ownership before accepting ADR 0005; proposed choices must remain explicitly unresolved.
evidence: ADR 0001 specifies attempt identity, actor/channel scope, sole orchestration writer, copied boundaries, lifecycle/outcomes, initial resource limits, cancellation, volatile state, and compatibility/rollback requirements.

ADR 0002 separates provider, domain-policy, and workflow responsibilities and specifies lifecycle/API versions, legacy Feeds/Knowledge adapters, preserved legacy overrides, atomic versioned registration, deterministic bindings, and explicit fallback.

ADR 0003 preserves current repositories/caches and the canonical stateless-service rule; the volatile prototype adds no persistence, and any broader rule/storage change remains an explicit later decision.

ADR 0004 defines a 30-day explicit hashtag-feedback target, original baseline and frozen snapshots, unscored/unknown/ambiguous outcomes, controlled single-attempt attribution, scope/estimator limitations, and shadow-only evaluation.
The documentation index and capability map now link to the decision records and identify baseline capture as the next step.

ADR 0005 was withdrawn from accepted status and remains proposed. The follow-up research separates semantic, inference, runtime, and package dependencies; compares two compatible cycle owners; and distinguishes pre-action simulation from post-action observed learning using six primary/official sources.

ADR 0006 records the owner's decision that reading is one macro-component grown from Feeds, Knowledge stores content with provenance, Experience records the reading episode, and Book is not a service Extraction is the middle ground: Reading acquires and extracts into Knowledge's Extracted contract, Knowledge owns that contract plus chunking, embedding, storage and retrieval.

ADR 0007 records the owner's confirmation that macro-components are faculties (Reading, Knowledge, Experience, Prediction, Moderation, Attention, Language, Action, Coordination) and that Book, Meme and Digest are workflows over them; workflow recipes sequence and configure, faculty domains decide.

ADR 0007 resolves its questions with the owner: Moderation (admissibility) and Attention (priority) are separate faculties; the meme pool is a reading cache; workflows go from feature handlers to typed Go workflows to versioned recipes, with recipes as an outcome of migration.

Owner reopened cognitive allocation as a hypothesis on 2026-10-21. ADR 0005 preserves the historical prototype decision and adds a causal follow-up review proposal; see step 10.2. No final capability/deployment boundary is inferred.

steps.title: Evaluate the architecture and select the next migrations
acceptance_criteria: Existing behavior, workspace-only behavior, and shadow prediction are compared on fixed cases.
Coupling, fault containment, latency, resource use, and trace usefulness are assessed.
Prediction skill, support, and feedback coverage are reported without claiming evidence from insufficient data.
The remaining roadmap is revised from measured results before broad adoption.
evidence: Existing, workspace-only and shadow modes deliver identical text on 8 fixed cases; task modes give a stable reason for abstention, unreadable media, Knowledge outage and degraded prediction where the existing path only logs or swallows it.

Workspace overhead with instant fakes: about 5-140 us per delivery; trace 0.5-2.0 KB per attempt. Shadow waits for Memory up to the 1 s budget (100 ms, 400 ms, 1.000 s at a 2 s delay); the other modes do not wait.
Live memory.recall on the owner's running Memory service (read-only, 31 requests): warm p50 26 ms, p95 32 ms; cold 1305 ms, which misses the 1 s budget.
Coupling per experiment commit and fault containment recorded; no envelope, schema, existing route or interface command changed; rollback is one composition line per orchestrator experiment.
Real prediction data: 7 hashtag.suggest attempts scored (5 legacy path, 2 task path), 0 resolved over 5 days; Brier and skill not computable; feedback coverage 0/7.

Owner decisions: adopt the workspace for multi-faculty workflows, adopt the reading host, keep shadow prediction with a local agent CLI (Claude Code or Codex) before Ollama as direction, accept the latency budgets.

The Memory store now acknowledges only the winning verdict under concurrent writes. See dokja_docs/experience-feedback.md.

Desktop retains the row, explains setup, and waits to offer QR/routing controls until configured. Existing configured link/unlink flows are preserved.

2026-10-22: content acquisition now has versioned document.process.v1, media.library.v1 and media.perceive.v1 providers under Feeds. Book/Meme facades default to plugin transports, with legacy-content Compose rollback; scrapers use source.collect.v1 adapters. See dokja_docs/feeds-content-plugins.md. substeps.title: Manage optional runtime modules from desktop on demand
deliverables: Module inventory with runtime backend, required dependencies and lifecycle ownership
Minimal control-plane bootstrap and per-module start/stop integration through the orchestrator
Desktop lifecycle states, startup failures and regression coverage
acceptance_criteria: Opening the desktop does not start the entire stack. Optional modules may remain off by default; selecting On starts only the selected module and its required dependencies.
Define the minimal control-plane bootstrap needed to start modules without requiring the full application stack to be running.

Separate logical routing enablement from actual process/container lifecycle. Report starting, ready, stopping, stopped and failed states; a successful switch alone must not imply that the module is running.
Enable module use only after readiness succeeds; expose actionable startup errors and allow an explicit retry without starting unrelated modules.
Define Off behavior and dependency ownership explicitly. Stopping one module must preserve dependencies still used by another active module and retain persistent data.
Keep Interface -> Event/Request -> Orchestrator -> Domain -> Service. The renderer requests module actions; domain-owned lifecycle policy and bounded runtime adapters perform them.

Specify the execution backend per module, including Compose containers and host-run components where applicable, before implementation. Preserve existing public contracts or review their compatibility explicitly.

Test startup from a stopped module, readiness timeout/failure, repeated requests, independent modules and shared dependencies. Update affected compose files and the production runbook with configuration changes.
evidence: Implemented a host background bootstrap orchestrator, Runtime domain and stateless Compose adapter. Desktop starts only the daemon on a runtime read; explicit module actions start/stop only dependency closures. Readiness and background failures are visible even with the main orchestrator stopped.

Initial selectable lite modules: orchestrator, Memory, Knowledge, Meme, Book, Chat AI, Feeds, Voice and WhatsApp. Shared and borrowed dependencies, recognized external consumers, data, auth and history volumes are preserved. One operation runs at a time; ownership survives daemon restart; application acknowledgements gate ready state.

Private Unix socket, OS instance lock, project-bound protocol responses and real-input IPC validation bound the local control surface. Existing routing switches stay separate. Windows, production and remote/custom orchestrator endpoints are outside the initial backend.

System UI consolidates lifecycle and activity into one module row. Optional request handling and WhatsApp setup stay under module options; automation remains in the same card. Regression coverage includes controller-unavailable fallback.

Provider inspection found that the local Docker-compatible CLI ignores DOCKER_HOST under Podman. The adapter bridges an explicit local Unix socket into CONTAINER_HOST when no Podman override is present, so it addresses the configured engine rather than an unrelated container context.
